summary: SpaceX (Grok/xAI compute) is significantly undervalued in public markets; the compute buildout optionality is not in estimates
summary_extended: Baker argues that SpaceX is significantly undervalued in public markets because consensus estimates (~$73B revenue for next year) do not price in the optionality of a massive compute buildout that could reach 8 gigawatts of capacity. He notes SpaceX has demonstrated the ability to deploy compute faster and at lower cost than anyone except the hyperscalers, and is monetizing at roughly $50B per gigawatt, meaning even a fraction of the reported 8GW target would be transformative to the valuation. Baker is skeptical of the exact 8GW figure from the Funder AI Substack report but emphasizes that the market is focused on a bear case (spot inference prices down ~90%) while ignoring the supply-side buildout optionality entirely. He also flags the Star Cloud orbital compute partnership as an additional underappreciated call option on the business. The investment implication is that SpaceX shares (accessible only in private markets) are mispriced to the downside, with Grok 4.5 and the Cursor acquisition having materially improved fundamentals since IPO.
